In these appeals, the appellants have challenged the judgment dated 16.11.2019 passed in M.V.C.No.554/2017 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal at Raichur (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal' for short).

sentences.text: The parties will be referred with respect to their status before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
4. Briefly stated the facts are that, petitioner Nos.1 and 2 are the parents and petitioner No.3 is the sister of one Kashyap, the deceased.

On 24.09.2017, the deceased while returning along with his fiance Kum.Ajitha from Hampi to Hyderabad near Raghavendra Brick Factory on Micro Tower Yermarus Road in Raichur taluk, met with an accident due to hit by a lorry bearing No.AP-31/TF-5249 coming in the opposite direction.
Consequently, the deceased sustained severe head injury, fracture of right hand, right thigh and abdominal injuries.

He was taken to RIMS,
Raichur, then while on the transit to Hyderabad hospital, he died.

5. Deceased was aged 27 years, B.Tech. graduate from International Institute of Information and Technology (IIIT), Hyderabad, was working in Microsoft India (R&D) Pvt.Ltd., Hyderabad, earning annual salary of Rs.21,06,089/-.

entities.text: International Institute of Information and Technology (IIIT), Hyderabad
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On these grounds, the petitioners moved the Tribunal seeking award of compensation of Rs.4,95,50,000/-.

The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company on the ground that the accident occurred due to complete negligence on the part of the deceased, that he drove the car from the opposite direction and hit against the lorry and that he was not earning as claimed by the petitioners.
The Tribunal awarded Rs.3,66,31,169/- and directed the Insurance Company to deposit 75% and deducted 25% towards contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.

Pleading inadequacy of compensation and attribution of contributory negligence were incorrect, the petitioners are before this Court whereas, the Insurance Company aggrieved by the direction of depositing 75% of compensation and assessment of compensation was on higher side is also before this court in the connected appeal.

6. Heard the arguments of Sri.Babu H.Metagudda, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri.Manvendra Reddy, learned counsel for the Insurance Company and perused the records.
7.
According to the learned counsel for petitioners, the deceased was a Software Engineer working in Microsoft Company, Hyderabad and drawing annual salary of Rs.40 lakhs.

The accident occurred due to complete negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry and therefore, the attribution of contributory negligence of 25% is not correct and sought for re- assessment of compensation.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company contended that, as per the statement of income-tax filed under Ex.P23, the income of the deceased was not Rs.40 lakhs or Rs.30,72,368/- as claimed by the petitioners or even Rs.21,06,089/-.
After excluding the tax component, if loss of dependency is computed, it will not come to Rs.3,66,31,169/- and therefore, the assessment of compensation is not proper and it requires to be modified.

It is also contended that the accident occurred due to sheer negligence of deceased, attribution of 75% of contributory negligence against the lorry is not proper and hence urged for reducing the extent of his contribution to the happening of the accident.
9. We have given our anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and perused the impugned judgment.

sentences.text:
As seen from the entire material on record, we notice that there is no dispute as to the accident,
cause of accident, injuries sustained by the deceased and death due to injuries.
The petitioners being the parents and sister are the dependants and are entitled to claim compensation.

11. The contention of the Insurance Company that future prospects of 50% taken is not proper and in this regard, law is settled in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others 2017 ACJ 680.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others 2017 ACJ 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For the age below 40 years and a person having a permanent employment, the future prospects has to be considered at 50%, and 40% if he is self-employed or on a fixed salary.

12. Here, in this case, the material on record does point out that the deceased was a graduate of B.Tech. (Computer Science) from IIIT, Hyderabad; he was employed in Microsoft (India) Co.Ltd.,
Hyderabad, since 24.08.2015 and he had been paid a handful of salary.
In this regard, Ex.P21 is the salary details of the deceased provided by Microsoft India (R&D) Private Limited, for the period from 01.04.2017 to 24.09.2017, which was for the relevant point of time.
Ex.P23 is the Income-Tax returns pertaining to the deceased indicating that he was aged 27 years old, employed in M/s.Microsoft India (R&D) Private Limited and he was paid Rs.30,72,368/-.

What has also been noticed by us is that, for the months of April to September 2017, the deceased received the salary and thereafter there was no salary paid to him.
13.

We have carefully perused Ex.P21 and Ex.P23, which clearly point out the salary calculation for the month of April 2017 - Rs.1,45,128/-; May 2017 - Rs.1,47,226/-; June 2017 - 1,45,128/-; July - 1,48,128/-; August - 1,48,128/-; September - Rs.3,65,111/- and October - Rs.2,46,508/-, with average of monthly Tax deduction of Rs.24,767/-.

We have also noticed that though a sum of Rs.3,65,111/- was paid as salary in the month of September 2017, it included the Performance Bonus of Rs.1,84,400/-, Stock Vest Perquisite Rs.47,381/- paid on account of death of the deceased.
In the month of October 2017, Stock Vest Perquisite of Rs.2,45,604/- was paid to the parents of the deceased.

In the month of February 2018,
Rs.12,39,220/- was paid towards gratuity and death benefits.
If all these aspects have been taken into consideration, the total income will come to Rs.30,72,368/-, which the Tribunal has taken as the income and calculated the loss of dependency.

14. On a careful evaluation of the statement of income, we notice that a sum of Rs.3,65,111/- and Rs.2,46,508/-, which were paid to the deceased in the months of September and October 2017 and also Rs.12,39,220/- in the month of February 2018, were not the salary but they were death benefits.

We are constrained to calculate the average salary of the deceased taking into consideration the salary for the months of April 2017 to September 2017, i.e., for five months, which maintained the uniformity throughout.
If that calculation is made, the salary of the deceased comes to Rs.17,60,976/- per annum whereas, tax component comes to Rs.2,97,204/-.

The net income means the income excluding the tax as laid down in Pranay Sethi's case (supra) and also the multiplier applicable for the age of '27' as per Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation (2009)6 SCC 121, is '17'.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation (2009)6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, we assess the annual income of the deceased at Rs.17,60,976/- minus Rs.2,97,204/- =
Rs.14,63,772/-.
Since the deceased was a bachelor, 50% has to be deducted towards personal expenses.

Since the deceased was in a permanent employment in Microsoft India (R&D) Private Sri. Kompella Venkat Rao And Ors vs Sri. Md. Prasad Raju And Ors on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120049370/
5 Limited, future prospects has to be considered at 50%, having regard to the performance bonus paid to him in the month of September 2017.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, the computation of loss of dependency would be:
Rs.14,63,772/- + 50% (Rs.7,31,886/-) comes to Rs.21,95,658/-.
If 50% is excluded towards his personal expenses, income would come to Rs.10,97,829/- and if multiplied by '17', it comes to Rs.1,86,63,093/-.

Since the deceased left behind his parents and sister, towards loss of love and affection, a sum of Rs.40,000/- each;
towards funeral expenses and loss of estate, Rs.15,000/- each if assessed under conventional heads, the total compensation comes to Rs.1,88,13,093/- as against Rs.3,66,31,169/- assessed by the Tribunal.

Therefore, we find that the compensation assessed by the Tribunal is not in accordance with the evidence placed before it and for this reason, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal needs to be modified, as it is excessive.

15. As regards contributory negligence is concerned, we have considered the materials on record,
particularly, the spot mahazar-cum-sketch at Ex.P2, wherein the Investigating Officer has specifically recorded the topography of the place of accident. As seen from the sketch, at the place of accident, the width of the road was 30 feet whereas the car was going towards Hyderabad side,
which was 8 feet inside the road from the left side of the road, whereas the lorry, which was going on the opposite direction, had crossed the middle lane of 15 feet and gone 7 feet further more towards right side while hitting the car. The Tribunal has rightly made an assessment that, if the deceased was careful in driving the car, he could have avoided the accident.

Ex.P7 is the photo of the lorry,
which points out that the right front portion of the lorry had hit against the right front portion of the car, which clearly indicates negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry.
Also we can see the photographs of the car at Exs.P11 to P14, which indicate damage on the right front portion of the car.
Therefore, the attribution of contributory negligence on the part of the deceased is rightly assessed by the Tribunal.

16. The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that there is no negligence on the part of the deceased cannot be accepted and at the same time, the contention of the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that equal contributory negligence has to be attributed against the deceased also cannot be supported with.

Therefore, we are of the considered opinion that contributory negligence on the part of the lorry was 80% and that of the deceased was 20%.
17.

On a careful evaluation of the materials on record, we stand in support of the opinion of the Tribunal as to the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased to the extent of 20% only and that of the driver of the lorry at 80% and accordingly, the assessed compensation has to be apportioned to the petitioners.

18. In the result, we pass the following;
ORDER (i) M.F.A.No.200339/2020 filed by the petitioners is allowed in part.
